title: PowerPoint (Desktop): reference SharePoint and OneDrive files when creating a presentation with Copilot Agent Mode
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, file-reference behaviour and documented governance controls are supported. The SharePoint path and PowerShell command match Microsoft's instructions, and the briefing keeps feature-specific licensing, metering and default-state gaps explicit.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes referencing files in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation using Agent Mode in PowerPoint.
claims.quote: You can now reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Copilot using Agent Mode in PowerPoint.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Copilot in PowerPoint recognises a SharePoint or OneDrive file mentioned by file or document name in a prompt.
claims.quote: Copilot in PowerPoint can now recognize references to files stored in SharePoint and OneDrive when you mention them in your prompt, such as by file or document name.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance
claims.claim: A prompt can identify the file by document owner as well as document name.
claims.quote: In your prompt, reference a file saved in SharePoint or OneDrive by the document name and/or owner of the document.

claims.claim: Users need not manually attach or upload the referenced file.
claims.quote: This update makes it easier to use relevant Microsoft 365 content without manually attaching or uploading the file.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot can use the referenced file as context to create a presentation containing information from it.
claims.quote: You can naturally reference a relevant file in your prompt, and Copilot can use that file as context when creating your presentation.

claims.quote: Previously, these implicit file references were not supported for files stored in these locations.

claims.claim: The release notes describe a general gradual rollout from a subset of tenant users to the organisation.

claims.claim: The release notes give no rollout schedule specific to this feature.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference files SharePoint OneDrive implicit file references admin setting disable default Graph policy; opened release notes introduction and full October 06 file-reference entry: no feature-specific rollout schedule.

claims.where: summary; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions and references content the user is authorised to access.
claims.quote:
Copilot only summarizes or references content that the user is already authorized to access.
Copilot respects existing SharePoint and OneDrive permissions.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot can surface already overshared content to users who have access.
claims.quote: If content is already overshared, Copilot can surface it to anyone who has access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Copilot honours sensitivity labels and encryption when grounding responses and generating content.
claims.quote: Copilot honors Microsoft Purview sensitivity labels and encryption when it grounds responses and generates content.

claims.claim: Subject to the stated exceptions, Copilot and agents cannot access unopened SharePoint and OneDrive documents labelled and encrypted with user-defined permissions.
claims.quote: Copilot and agents can't access unopened documents in SharePoint and OneDrive that are labeled and encrypted with user-defined permissions.

claims.claim: A default sensitivity label extending SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents is one exception to that restriction.
claims.quote: There are two exceptions: the label is a default sensitivity label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents, or the user references the document directly by typing "/".

claims.claim: A user directly referencing the document by typing slash is the other exception.
claims.quote: There are two exceptions: the label is a default sensitivity label that extends SharePoint permissions to downloaded documents, or the user references the document directly by typing "/".

claims.claim: The user must also have the EXTRACT usage right in both exceptions.
claims.quote: In both cases, the user must also have the EXTRACT usage right.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; Governance controls
claims.claim: A DLP policy for Copilot can prevent summarisation of labelled files.
claims.quote: A DLP policy for Copilot can keep Copilot from summarizing labeled files and emails.

claims.claim: A DLP policy for Copilot can prevent summarisation of labelled emails.
claims.quote: A DLP policy for Copilot can keep Copilot from summarizing labeled files and emails.

claims.claim: Sensitivity-label-based DLP blocking of file processing is documented for Copilot in PowerPoint.
claims.quote:
Block files and emails with sensitivity labels from being processed
This feature is available in Microsoft 365 Copilot, Copilot Chat, Cowork, and Copilot in Word, Excel, and PowerPoint.

claims.claim: Items protected by this DLP control may still appear in citations.
claims.quote: Identified items still appear in the citations of the response, but Copilot and Cowork don't access or use the content of the item in the response.

claims.claim: Copilot does not use the protected item's content in the response.
claims.quote: Identified items still appear in the citations of the response, but Copilot and Cowork don't access or use the content of the item in the response.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery limits SharePoint content in organisation-wide search and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including tenant-wide discovery.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery affects organization-wide search experiences (SharePoint home, Office.com, Bing) and Microsoft Copilot discovery scenarios, including experiences that rely on tenant-wide content discovery.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery does not change existing permissions.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery doesn't change existing permissions.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery leaves existing users' direct access to content intact.
claims.quote: Users who already have access to content can continue to access that content directly.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery is a general SharePoint site-level control rather than a setting specific to PowerPoint file references.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is a site-level setting. When you turn on the setting, Microsoft 365 search systems propagate it so that content from the site doesn't appear in organization-wide discovery experiences.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes Restricted Content Discovery as intended for Copilot deployment and governance scenarios.
claims.quote: Restricted Content Discovery is intended for Microsoft Copilot deployment and governance scenarios.

claims.claim: Restricted Content Discovery changes can take time to propagate through search and Copilot experiences.
claims.quote: Updates can take time to propagate throughout search and Microsoft Copilot experiences.

claims.claim: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.
claims.quote: By default, only SharePoint administrators can manage Restricted Content Discovery.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The setting is at SharePoint admin center > Sites > Active sites > site > Settings > Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot.
claims.quote:
In the SharePoint admin center, expand Sites and select Active sites.
Select the site you want to configure.
Open the Settings tab, and then turn Restrict content from Microsoft Copilot on.

claims.claim: Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true enables Restricted Content Discovery on a site.
claims.quote:
Enable Restricted Content Discovery for a site
Use PowerShell
Set-SPOSite -Identity <site-url> -RestrictContentOrgWideSearch $true

claims.claim: The Microsoft Copilot overview describes Premium as the add-on licensed full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint and OneNote.
claims.quote: You have the Microsoft 365 Copilot add-on license with access to the full experience of Copilot in Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and OneNote.

claims.claim: The overview also documents Basic users without the add-on being able to use Copilot in these apps.

claims.claim: The release notes entry describes no action taken on the source file.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot PowerPoint reference files SharePoint OneDrive implicit file references admin setting disable default Graph policy. Read the full release entry: it describes referencing a file and creating a presentation, with no action on the source file.

claims.claim: The release notes entry describes no write access to SharePoint or OneDrive.
claims.quote: Searched: Microsoft Graph PowerShell disable implicit SharePoint OneDrive file references Copilot PowerPoint. Opened the full release entry: no SharePoint or OneDrive write access is described for this capability.

claims.claim: The supplied roadmap record does not name a licence for the feature.
claims.quote: "description": "You can now reference files saved in SharePoint libraries and OneDrive folders when creating a presentation with Copilot using Agent Mode in PowerPoint."
